identity.title: Detection of Infall in the Protostar B335 with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: Observations of the isolated globule B335 with ALMA have yielded absorption features against the continuum that are redshifted from the systemic velocity in both HCN and HCO$^+$ lines.

question.value: Is there unambiguous infall toward the Class 0 protostar B335, seen as redshifted absorption against the continuum, and can an inside-out collapse model reproduce the HCN and HCO+ profiles?

evidence.quote: Our goal is to see if a previously developed physical model can account approximately for the observed line profiles.
Observations of B335 were obtained as part of project 2012.1.00346.S (PI. N. Evans) on 27 April 2014 (UT)
The observations used 35 12-m antennas and the Band 7 receivers.

method.value: Polynomial fit to line-free channels, subtracted in image plane to avoid artifacts with absorption

method.value: 2D Gaussian fit to continuum; spectra from 0.5"x0.5" box on source and 0.5" circles north/south as off-source check; converted to TR

validation.value: Off-source spectra show no absorption below the continuum, confirming absorption confined to the continuum source

evidence.quote: While red-shifted **self**-absorption can be seen, the lines no longer show significant absorption below the continuum.

analysis_steps.goal: Model line profiles with inside-out collapse

method.value: Shu inside-out collapse with dust and gas thermal codes, Monte Carlo radiative transfer, beam 0.57", 80 shells with inner radius 6 AU, central continuum source, baseline removal; abundance profiles (step for HCO+, drop for HCN) tuned

evidence.loc: 4.2 Simple Models of Line Emission: Pure Infall
evidence.quote: we have doubled the number of shells (to 80) in the radiative transport code, extending the inner radius of the model to 6 AU.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN and HCO+ show redshifted absorption against the continuum; CS shows red self-absorption but no absorption below the continuum; H13CN shows none

evidence.quote: The H$^{13}$CN spectrum shows no absorption feature.

claims.experiment: Spectra of four lines extracted toward the continuum peak and off-source
claims.result: Redshifted absorption below the continuum in HCN and HCO+ on source only
claims.finding: Infall is clearly detected via the inverse P-Cygni signature

evidence.quote: infall has been clearly detected in the HCN and HCO$^+$ lines via the IPC signature.

claims.hypothesis: Can the inside-out collapse model match the profiles?
claims.experiment: Model with r_inf = 0.012 pc compared to ALMA spectra
claims.result: Reasonably good fit of peaks, absorption dip and wings, with tuned abundances
claims.finding: Infall radius 0.012 pc, rate 3e-6 Msun/yr, age 5e4 yr

evidence.loc: 4.2 Simple Models of Line Emission: Pure Infall
evidence.quote: The model produces a reasonably good fit to the double-peaked lines, the absorption dip, and even the line wings.

claims.hypothesis: Is much mass in an optically thin disk?
claims.finding: Disk mass is very small; most accumulated mass is in the star or opaque regions

evidence.quote: consistent with only a very small disk mass.

why_this_method.value: Absorption against continuum gives unambiguous infall evidence; high resolution excludes outflow

evidence.quote: Another advantage of very high spatial resolution is that the outflow region may be excluded

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Unrelated foreground layer as the absorber is rejected given B335's isolation and high lower-state energies

evidence.quote: The simplicity and isolation of the B335 globule (cite: 2007A&A...475..281G) make this explanation highly unlikely

limitations_admitted.value: Simple spherical models do not perfectly match; abundance profiles are ad hoc

evidence.loc: 4.2 Simple Models of Line Emission: Pure Infall
